text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Automated alert: KV eviction rate for cluster rope-pool-3 exceeded threshold (evictions/sec > 12) and continuous-batching queue depth jumped. Routing to #incidents for triage. dashboard: https://redwood.ops/alerts/2037671110

maria: I'm seeing p95/p99 token latency climb for long-context routes (ntk-long-read). Errors are decode/timeout spikes, mostly 503s from the serving layer.

ajay: taking lead. pinging SRE oncall. any recent deploys to rope or batching config?

lucas: no infra deploys in last 30m. Model/rope config update rolled 2h ago that extended sliding window span to 8k tokens for some customers (A/B). suspect interaction with continuous batching + KV footprint.

bethany: can we confirm KV cardinality? prefix key counts look abnormal for that pool, lots of unique prefixes from the long-window requests. may be cache blowup due to larger prefixes (NTK change).

maria: customer-ops, any customers reporting errors?

customer-ops: seeing support tickets from two customers (acme & polaris). Both report elevated latencies and transient failures on large-context summaries. impact: ~12% of requests for those routes return 5xx.

ajay: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle long-context routes (route-level qps cap) 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for rope-pool-3 3) reduce sliding-window span from 8k->4k for canary cohort 4) increase KV eviction aggressiveness. I'm going to run the commands.

lucas: agree. recommend also setting temporary fallback to shorter-context model variant to avoid huge KV allocations.

maria: ajay, share commands you'll run so we can review before applying.

ajay: running now. commands:
```bash
# throttle route
redwoodctl routes update ntk-long-read --max-qps 60 --cluster rope-pool-3

# disable continuous batching on cluster
redwoodctl cluster config set rope-pool-3 continuous_batch.enabled false

# adjust sliding window for canary users
redwoodctl featureflag set ntk-long-window-size 4096 --target=canary

# bump kv eviction pressure
redwoodctl kv settings rope-pool-3 --eviction-threshold 0.75 --ttl 900
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: cluster-config-change by ajay (CID: d3f4a9). Logs: https://redwood.ops/deploys/d3f4a9

maria: applying throttle, patching cluster config now. will monitor metrics.

(3m later)

lucas: early telemetry: eviction rate down 60%, continuous-batching queue depth normalized. p99 latency decreasing but still above baseline by ~25%. error rate for long-context routes down from 12% -> 2.1%.

bethany: good. we should keep throttle + disable for 30m then re-evaluate. also need to capture a heap snapshot of KV usage for postmortem. @deploy-bot can you capture?

deploy-bot: KV heap snapshot initiated on rope-pool-3 (snapshot id: snap-2037671110-1).

customer-ops: notified affected customers with mitigation ETA. support doc: https://redwood.support/longctx-incident-2037671110

ajay: scheduling handoff — I'm primary for next 20m, after that lucas takes oncall for follow-through and postmortem.

maria: lucas please confirm you can take over at +20m. also create incident page in opsbook with timelines & config diffs.

lucas: confirm. will create opsbook page and start collecting diffs. I'll also pull sample request traces for the canary cohort.

(18m later)

lucas: taking over. summary so far: root cause likely amplification of KV keys by extending sliding window (NTK/YaRN semantics) combined with continuous-batching aggregation that preserved many unique prefixes in KV. That increased memory & eviction pressure, causing thrashing which then produced timeouts.

bethany: agree with root cause hypothesis. action items for postmortem: - rollback sliding-window change for all cohorts - add guardrails in release process to flag KV cardinality risk - instrument per-route KV key cardinality metrics - autoscale eviction pressure when unique-key growth > threshold

maria: customers are stable. recommended post-incident latency SLO check in 48h during normal traffic.

ajay: quick note for follow-up: evaluate whether continuous-batching should have per-route key deduplication or per-request prefix hashing to limit KV expansion. add to research backlog.

lucas: creating the incident ticket now with timeline, config diffs, snapshots and impacted customers. ticket: https://redwood.ops/incidents/2037671110/postmortem

oncall-rotation: handoff acknowledged. lucas is oncall. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

(1h later)

maria: closing incident as mitigated. keeping an eye on the cluster. will convene postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PT.

incident-bot: Incident resolved (2037671110). Summary: mitigations applied (route throttle, disable continuous batching, reduce sliding window for canary, increased eviction). Final metrics: eviction rate normalized, error rate -> 0.5% on affected routes, p99 latency within 10% of baseline. Links: opsbook and snapshots above.
